findings.evidence: src/workflow/artifacts/companion/shell.ts:217 `export function renderCompanionPage(header: CompanionHeader, page: CompanionPageContent, runtime: CompanionRuntime): string`; src/docgen/render/shell.ts:259-262 `export async function assembleShell(ir: DocumentIR, renderer: SubprocessRenderer = graphvizSubprocessRenderer): Promise<DocGenOutcome<RenderedDocumentShell>>`. findings.premise: The change-site inventory (§3.1, listing only companion/shell.ts, docgen/render/shell.ts and docgen/render/fallback.ts as call sites) is complete for a single shared `DIAGRAM_OVERRIDES_CSS` string to apply correctly in both shells.
findings.evidence: The companion shell wraps the rendered diagram in `<div class="stage" id="stage">` (src/workflow/artifacts/companion/shell.ts:251), while docgen's primary and fallback shells wrap it in `<div id="docgen-diagram">` (src/docgen/render/shell.ts:235 and src/docgen/render/fallback.ts:242) — two different container selectors. The design's own reference override CSS [[c5]] (docs/previews/mermaid-themes/insors-diagram-overrides.css) is scoped to `.stage svg .relationshipLabel`/`.relationshipLabelBox`, which only matches the companion shell's DOM. The LLD never lists a DOM-harmonization change (a shared wrapper class/id) to either shell as part of §3.1's call sites, so a single DIAGRAM_OVERRIDES_CSS string built on that reference would silently fail to apply in the docgen shells, reproducing exactly the R3 ER-contrast defect the story exists to fix in one of the two rendering paths. [files: src/workflow/artifacts/companion/shell.ts, src/docgen/render/shell.ts, src/docgen/render/fallback.ts, docs/previews/mermaid-themes/insors-diagram-overrides.css]
findings.action: Read the exact container markup in all three shell/fallback files and the reference override CSS, and compared selectors.

findings.premise: No stored/persisted shape needs migration — `RenderedDocumentShell` stays structurally unchanged and old generated HTML files are plain static files with no versioned record to migrate, matching the LLD's 'Zero downtime: yes — Data rewrite: no'.
findings.evidence: src/docgen/types.ts:125-132 `RenderedDocumentShell { docType, backend, html, inlinedRuntimeVersion, diagramFormat:'svg', supportsZoomPan:true }` has no versioned/stored field that the new theme policy would need to add or migrate; a generated artifact is a single self-contained .html file on disk, not a database row, so 'old saved HTML stays readable' requires no code migration path, only that generation code keeps emitting a valid self-contained file (which it already does). [files: src/docgen/types.ts]
findings.action: Read the RenderedDocumentShell type definition and confirmed artifacts are plain HTML files, not DB-backed records.

findings.evidence: plans/mermaid-theme-and-readability-requirements.md's NFR1 row explicitly requires measuring 'actual theme pairs in representative rendered states'. hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone triage-routed feature story (no HLD): scope is the two artifact rendering shells + a new shared theme module + the asset pipeline.

boundary.internal: Shared Insors-branded light/dark Mermaid theme policy consumed by companion shell (src/workflow/artifacts/companion/shell.ts) and docgen shell (src/docgen/render/shell.ts + fallback.ts), with Poppins packaged under src/assets/fonts and shipped by copy-assets.mjs.

nonFunctional.security: strict Mermaid securityLevel retained; no author-supplied CSS/JS/config executed; no remote URL in artifacts (NFR6/NFR3)

summary.prose: This story adds one versioned Insors-branded theme policy module for generated Mermaid artifacts and makes both rendering shells (workflow companions and docgen) consume it: brand palette with coordinated light/dark variants, packaged Poppins, ER label contrast overrides, readable initial scale with fit as a separate action, theme toggle, SVG export, and honest error states — all offline, strict Mermaid security unchanged.

migration.stateAfter: Both shells inline the shared branded theme policy (light/dark), packaged Poppins, overrides, viewer controls and a theme version stamp. Existing saved artifacts are not rewritten.
